key_insight: Wonder turns a single image or conditional video into an interactive, real-time "playable world" that users can explore by moving the camera. Its main breakthrough is a system-level design that combines control, memory, and training so the world remains coherent over both short and long horizons.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of building a general-purpose video world model that supports camera-controllable exploration in real time, while still remembering previously seen areas and generating plausible unseen regions.
method: Introduces a camera-control mechanism that lets users navigate the generated world interactively.
Uses a memory mechanism to preserve and revisit previously observed content during long-term exploration.
Co-designs the training strategy with the control and memory components to improve realism, consistency, and responsiveness.
impact: This matters because it moves video world models closer to practical, interactive tools for simulation, content creation, and embodied AI research. For practitioners, it suggests a scalable way to build more controllable and persistent generative environments.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing input image/video transforming into a navigable world
Camera movement path overlay illustrating user-controlled exploration
Memory map or timeline showing revisited regions staying consistent over time
System architecture block diagram highlighting control, memory, and training modules
paper_title: Wonder: Video World Model Done Better
paper_authors: Jiacong Xu, Hanwen Jiang, Zhixin Shu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Vishal M. Patel
